commits.message:
Refuse a validation-trace VerifySource that does not spend its pending claim

Adds a funding-permit row presenting VerifySource with the pending claim
left out of its spent inputs; the permit must refuse it as omitting its
pending claim.

Give each pass's held-event retry to the least recently retried hold

The per-pass retry slot went to the first due held event in step order,
so a later held event could wait while an earlier one kept failing. The
slot now goes to the block's due hold that failed least recently, with
ties in step order, so every hold is retried within a bounded number of
passes.

Resolve validation-trace removal contracts as deployed and forget completed removals

The conviction row now removes the block through the production
removal-contract resolution for 00000006, re-derived from the deployment's
dispute bond and case-configuration one-shot, with no resolution stub.
A block's removal adapter is forgotten once its removal is complete or in
conflict; a later observation rebuilds it from the L1 view, as after a
restart.

Reuse the detector's pre-state ledger for validation-trace claims

Claim preparation and artifact validation read the ledger the detector
walked to before a failing event, kept per evidence object and per event,
instead of walking the block's steps from the predecessor again. A claim
prepared from another predecessor, or for an event the detector did not
keep, walks as before.

Bound the retry work of held validation-trace re-executions

One replay pass re-executes at most one held event and carries any other
due one, still held, to the next pass. A hold forgotten past the
replayer's capacity keeps its retry time and attempt count in a fixed-size
backlog, so it is never retried sooner or backed off less. An event whose
re-execution fails the same way five times in a row is named stuck, its
own readiness reason, with one alert on entry; it keeps retrying at the
capped backoff, is never a verdict, and clears once it re-executes to an
outcome.

Cover each validation-trace dispute funding guard on its own

Adds refusal rows for the bond marker and case token units, the pending
claim's output bytes and out-ref, a second case output, a bond or case
output without its own token, an action other than the one the
reservation began, and a claim for another header. Drops two checks the
permit already enforces elsewhere: the opener-spent binding (the claim
lookup refuses an unspent claim) and the released-custody equality (the
claim is the only contract input admitted, and the runtime custody bound
covers the rest).

Refuse a validation-trace dispute authority bound to other bond or case terms

Adds funded refusal rows for a VerifySource whose authority and outputs
agree with each other but not with the deployment's dispute terms: a bond
above the deployment-bound bond, and the bond or the case paid to, and
bound at, another dispute contract. Each row stalls with its named binding.

Cover the validation-trace dispute's Open shortfall and shaped-coin funding

Under the watcher's prover funding, a wallet emptied after Init pauses
the objective at Open on the funding-shortfall hold on every observation,
releases the paused attempt's inputs, and Opens and VerifySources after a
top-up. A wallet whose ada sits in coins carrying an inline datum, a
datum hash or a reference script pauses VerifySource as an underfunded
one does, and none of those coins is ever spent or offered as
collateral.

Build the validation-trace pre-state ledger once per block

The validation-trace replay rebuilt each Plutus event's pre-state from the
predecessor ledger, re-checking every earlier step's committed root in
full. One walk of the block's steps now serves all of its events in step
order, and a step's root check reuses the descriptors of entries the
previous checked ledger already holds byte for byte. Results and refusals
are unchanged; a step whose root does not open refuses every later event
while earlier ones still decide.

Block replay at 10k predecessor entries: 10.7 s to 0.85 s (four passing
events), 15.8 s to 5.9 s (two failing). At 100k: 132 s to 10.9 s, and
219 s to 70 s.

Retry a validation-trace re-execution that fails without a verdict

Only a deterministic outcome without a verdict (a trace replay that
disagrees with the verdict, or a refused event pre-state) classifies the
block as an unprovable gap. An evaluator or store failure, including a
trace build stopped as unavailable, now holds only that event: it is
retried after a doubling backoff capped at 60 s, the block's other events
still replay, a failure proven on any of them decides the block, and
otherwise the replay throws ValidationTraceReplayHeldError naming the
validation_trace_replay_held readiness reason and its retry time.

The prepared artifact is accepted against any validation-trace detection
of the block, so a claim started while an earlier event was held stays
valid once that event resolves.

Remove the convicted block through the shared remove stage

Once our case's fraud-proof record is on chain, the validation-trace
runner hands the block to the shared cursor-family remove stage over the
family's authenticated raw-L1 observation, with the shared state-queue
mutation lease and the shared remove-fraudulent-block builder, instead of
raising validation-trace-case-convicted and waiting forever. The thread
token's path (opener, pending claim, case, proof token) is the family's
cursor spec; the case datum is read as a thread datum with its bounty
claimant as the fraud prover.

The convicted alarm now means only that the authenticated L1 view has not
yet seen the record. The conviction row runs to the authenticated
terminal: three removals (the two descendants, then the block), the
record kept, and the bond returned at close.

Cover the validation-trace runner's own outputs, landing and supersede rows

Look-alikes: exact copies and other shapes of the pending claim's datum,
planted at its contract before VerifySource is built, and of the case and
bond once the case is open, through the shared own-outputs harness.
VerifySource consumes the claim Open made, no transaction of ours touches
a plant, and a rerun over the open case submits nothing.

Under the watcher's prover funding: a larger token-bearing coin at the
prover address stays out of Init, Open and VerifySource; a process stopped
after its broadcast VerifySource landed sends nothing again; a stop before
broadcast supersedes the unsent bytes once they expire with one re-signed
attempt, after which the ledger refuses the stopped bytes. The case row
states that a production-built opener always clears the case floor.

Gate CEK and trace-commit scaling on semantic-store reads too

The hashed-bytes count cannot see super-linear work that hashes nothing, such as an unmemoised list walk. Both scaling gates now also count reads of the CEK semantic store (node, link, pairLink, blob) and allow at most 5% more per step at 2n than at n, on all 13 shapes. Removing the per-suffix size memo in MidgardCekSemanticSizing.sizedItems now turns mapData widening red in both gates (39.79 against a bound of 21.03 reads per step) while its hashing growth stays at 0.9998. Unchanged code measures 0.73 to 0.96.

The helper becomes measureWork in tests/helpers/work-count.ts and says what each counter counts and that only the non-gating bench sees work neither counts; the workflow marker reason says the same.

Hold only the event whose validation-trace re-execution ends in an error

A verdict replay with no verdict, or a trace build that fails for a
reason other than a stop, no longer fails the whole block's replay: the
event is named under validation-trace-replay-unavailable, an unregistered
id, so it classifies as an unprovable gap and the block still decides.
Rows inject the evaluator fault at the validation package; without it the
same block is the ordinary validation-trace fault.
